title: Session-rewindable canary lane with telemetry anchoring
author: Nina Park
description:
Context: We need a safer path for promoting shadow traffic to a canary that preserves session affinity and lets operators 'rewind' a partially promoted commit without a full rollback blast.
This PR introduces a rewindable canary lane that (1) supports session-affine traffic handover, (2) records compact model snapshot diffs to enable sub-minute rewinds, and (3) ties promotion gates to telemetry anchors (latency P95, error-rate, hallucination-rate) with configurable tolerances.
Motivations: nightly model churn and multi-variant A/B tests often surface regressions only after partial promotion and with session-affine state; current rollbacks are coarse-grained and can cause user-visible flips.
Design summary:
- New controller RewindableSwapController orchestrates staged promotions in small session-slice increments (configurable slice_size) and records an immutable promotion journal in object storage.
- Each promotion step emits a telemetry anchor snapshot (p95, error_rate, hallucination_rate, embedding-drift) and stores the snapshot alongside the snapshot-diff reference.
- Rewind operation replays the journal in reverse: it applies compact diffs to the serving plane and gracefully drains newly routed sessions.
- Session stickiness is preserved by a session-token mapping table; we add an optional session-migrate policy to migrate active sessions without a hard cutover.
- Safety gates are policy-driven: anchors must be within thresholds (defaults: p95 +10%, error_rate +0.5pp, hallucination_rate +1pp) for promotion to proceed.
- Developer ergonomics: CLI and Console integration for a one-click "rewind to N" with a preview of telemetry deltas.
What changed (high-level files):
- services/rollout-controller/controllers/rewindable_swap.py (controller + reconciliation loop)
- services/rollout-controller/api/v1alpha/rewindable_swap.proto (CRD/API)
- services/telemetry/anchors/anchor_probe.go (anchor snapshot and evaluation)
- docs/runbooks/release/rewindable-canary-playbook.md (operator playbook)
- console/components/canary/rewind-preview.tsx (UI preview)
- integration-tests/test_rewindable_canary.py (end-to-end tests)
Checklist:
- [x] Controller reconciliation and leader-election tested
- [x] Telemetry anchoring integrated with existing metrics pipeline
- [x] Integration tests covering promote/partial-promote/rewind
- [x] Console and CLI hooks included
- [x] Docs and runbook with step-by-step rewind guidance
Rollout plan: We will feature-flag the controller (feature.rewindable_canary = false by default). Deploy to staging for 48h, run synthetic smoke for 6 hours, then enable in canary region for a small internal cohort (1% sessions) before wider rollout.
Migration notes: Backwards compatible with existing Swap controller. If feature flag is disabled, behavior falls back to current atomic-swap.
Security: Journal objects are written to customer-specified object stores with ACLs; we reuse existing KMS envelope encryption.
Testing: Unit tests for diff application and rewind logic, integration tests that use a local object-store stub and simulated sessions, and end-to-end smoke in staging.
The CI pipeline initially failed on lint (prettier/flake8 infra) and a flaky telemetry assertion; both were addressed in followup commits and pipeline passed. See commits & conversation for details.
